learningObjective: Interpret L1/L2 cache hit-rate metrics in Nsight Compute and decide whether the metric points to a real optimization opportunity or is expected for the workload.
stem: Two elementwise FP32 kernels have identical implementations except for input size. Nsight Compute reports the following. Which conclusion is best supported?
profileData:
Kernel A: single-pass streaming over 1 GB (much larger than L2)
  L1 Hit Rate: 40 %
  L2 Hit Rate: 5 %
  DRAM Throughput: 92 %

Kernel B: single-pass streaming over 8 MB (fits in L2)
  L1 Hit Rate: 42 %
  L2 Hit Rate: 78 %
  DRAM Throughput: 22 %

options.text: Kernel A's low L2 hit rate is a bug; adding a shared-memory blocking scheme (loading tiles into shared memory) will let the L2 hit rate climb to Kernel B's level, unlocking a proportional speedup.
Kernel B is compute-bound because its DRAM throughput is only 22%; the correct optimization is to add more math per element to raise arithmetic intensity toward the ridge point of the roofline.

The L2 hit rates prove the L2 is unreliable on Ampere; disabling the L2 (via `cudaFuncSetAttribute` with CU_CTX_CACHE_L2_NONE) will make DRAM utilization consistent between the two kernels and improve total throughput.

Kernel A's low L2 hit rate is expected for a single-pass stream over data larger than L2 — each cache line is touched once and evicted before reuse. The kernel is memory-bound at 92% DRAM and shared-memory blocking cannot reduce the total number of unique bytes that must be read.

explanation: For a single-pass streaming kernel over data much larger than L2, cache is not reusable — the working set exceeds L2 capacity so lines are evicted before reuse. Low L2 hit rate is expected and not fixable by better locality. Kernel A's 92% DRAM utilization confirms it is near HBM peak. Blocking helps when there is reuse to expose, which is not the case here. Options A/B/C fabricate mechanisms: A misapplies blocking, B confuses low DRAM with compute-bound (it's simply that Kernel B mostly hits L2), C fabricates an L2-disable API.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: no data reuse to expose in a single-pass stream over data >> L2.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: Kernel B's low DRAM is because L2 is serving reads, not because it's compute-bound.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: disabling L2 is not a real optimization path.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: matches roofline / working-set analysis for streaming.

assumptions: A100 has ~40 MB L2 cache; 1 GB is well beyond it, 8 MB fits comfortably.
The elementwise kernel has no cross-element reuse in either case.
nonImplications: Does not imply cache-blocking is useless in general; it is critical for GEMM/attention where reuse exists.
Does not imply L2 hit rate is uninformative; combined with working-set size it is a meaningful diagnostic.

distractorRationales.A: Applies blocking where no reuse exists.

performanceClaim.scope: Single-pass streaming FP32 kernel over data larger vs smaller than L2 on A100
